## Course description

**Data Description** introduces the basic statistical tools
corresponding to the first stage of data analysis: numerical
summaries and graphical representation of data, computed hands-on in
Excel. By the end of the course, you will be able to take a raw
column of business data — sales, weather, customer counts — and turn
it into frequency tables, charts, and summary indicators that support
a real business decision. A single running case study, **"The
Wandering Fork"** (a fictional food-truck business), carries every
worked example from Session 3 onward, so results build on each other
across the whole course.

## Curriculum placement

This course is the natural sequel to **Mathematical Fundamentals
(MS01,** [`teaching/mathematical-fundamentals/`](../mathematical-fundamentals/index.qmd)**)**
and **Mathematical Analysis (MS02,**
[`teaching/mathematical-analysis/`](../mathematical-analysis/index.qmd)**)**,
and it is itself the prerequisite refresher for **Inferential
Statistics (MS04,**
[`teaching/decision-making-stat/`](../decision-making-stat/index.qmd)**)**,
whose own Session 6 explicitly revisits the numerical summaries
introduced here before moving on to confidence intervals and
hypothesis testing.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

1. Handle a spreadsheet fluently: cell referencing, sorting,
   PivotTables, and the basic Excel function library.
2. Identify the nature of a variable and build the correct frequency
   table and chart for it.
3. Compute and interpret position, central tendency, dispersion, and
   shape indicators for a quantitative variable.
4. Build and read a contingency table and a scatter plot for two
   variables observed together.
5. Compute and interpret covariance, correlation, and a simple
   linear regression line.
6. Reproduce every computation with the correct English-locale Excel
   function.

## Session outline

| Part | # | Session | Topic |
|---|---|---|---|
| I. Excel Fundamentals | 1 | [Session 1](session-01.qmd) | Excel Fundamentals I — cell referencing, basic functions |
| I. Excel Fundamentals | 2 | [Session 2](session-02.qmd) | Excel Fundamentals II — sorting, PivotTables, PivotCharts |
| II. Univariate Data Treatment | 3 | [Session 3](session-03.qmd) | Univariate graphical representation I — qualitative data |
| II. Univariate Data Treatment | 4 | [Session 4](session-04.qmd) | Univariate graphical representation II — quantitative data |
| II. Univariate Data Treatment | 5 | [Session 5](session-05.qmd) | Position indicators — quartiles, percentiles, boxplot |
| II. Univariate Data Treatment | 6 | [Session 6](session-06.qmd) | Central tendency — mean, median, mode |
| II. Univariate Data Treatment | 7 | [Session 7](session-07.qmd) | Dispersion — range, variance, standard deviation, CV |
| II. Univariate Data Treatment | 8 | [Session 8](session-08.qmd) | Asymmetry and shape — skewness |
| II. Univariate Data Treatment | 9 | [Session 9](session-09.qmd) | Univariate practical-work synthesis |
| III. Bivariate Data Treatment | 10 | [Session 10](session-10.qmd) | Bivariate graphical representation — contingency table, scatter plot |
| III. Bivariate Data Treatment | 11 | [Session 11](session-11.qmd) | Bivariate numerical summaries — covariance, correlation, regression |
| III. Bivariate Data Treatment | 12 | [Session 12](session-12.qmd) | Bivariate practical-work synthesis + mock exam |

**Part I** — Excel Fundamentals (Sessions 1–2, 6h) · **Part II** —
Univariate Data Treatment (Sessions 3–9, 18h) · **Part III** —
Bivariate Data Treatment (Sessions 10–12, 6h).

## Assessment

| Examination | % of overall grade | Assessment mode | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Midterm Exam (ME) | 35% | Individual written, MCQ component | 45 min |
| Final Exam (FE) | 65% | Individual written, MCQ component | 90 min |

Both exams cover Sessions 1–12; [Session 12](session-12.qmd) closes
the course with an original mock exam in the same format, for
self-assessment before the real thing.

## Personal work

**Volume**: 20 hours. Complete the exercises associated with each
part of the course (Excel Fundamentals, Univariate Data Treatment,
Bivariate Data Treatment) between sessions — every session page's
collapsible exercises are designed for exactly this.
